Pompey also gave Deiotarus of Galatia 'part of eastern Pontus' and Lesser Armenia (Deiotarus page), which is not cut out of this shape.

correction.text: the client kingdom plus Lesser Armenia and Colchis, ending in 62

region.text: a state in northern Cappadocia and eastern Paphlagonia round Amaseia

ledger.note: 281 BC: Mithridates I Ktistes proclaims himself king of Pontus. Infobox 'Established 281 BC'; 'in 281 (or 280) BC declared himself king of a state in northern Cappadocia and eastern Paphlagonia'. The page lists Amaseia and Sinope as capitals; Amasia was the early seat with the royal palace and tombs.

region.text: Amastris and the Paphlagonian coast west of the founding core

ledger.note: 279: Ariobarzanes takes Amastris. 'Ariobarzanes, Mithridates I's son, captured Amastris in 279 BC', the kingdom's first important Black Sea port; the page also has the kingdom expanding 'west to the river Sangrius'. Greek city taken as a port; the surrounding coast is the reading from Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the Greek city of Sinope

ledger.note: 183: Pharnaces I takes Sinope. 'It was not until 183 BC that Pharnaces reduced the Greek city of Sinope under their control.' The Kingdom of Pontus page puts the capture in 182; the Pharnaces I page's quoted sentence names no year for Sinope ('in which year he succeeded in reducing the important city of Sinope') and says only that he was 'on the throne before 183 BC'. Mithridates II had failed against Sinope c. 220.
183: Sinope becomes the Pontic capital. 'Sinope became the Pontic capital after its capture'; the infobox lists Amaseia and Sinope.

region.text: Cotyora, Pharnacia and Trapezus: 'most of the northern Anatolian coast' east of Sinope

ledger.note: 182: Pharnaces I takes the coast to Trapezus. 'Pharnaces I took Sinope. He also took Cotyora, Pharnacia, and Trapezus, gaining most of the northern Anatolian coast.' The year is the page's; the coastal belt is read from Cliopatria's -170 shape (37 cells, lon 35.0-40.5).

region.text: Galatia, where Pharnaces took territory in the early campaign (the page names no places)

ledger.note: 181: Pharnaces I attacks Pergamon and Cappadocia and invades Galatia. 'In spring 181 BC, Pharnaces attacked both Eumenes II of Pergamon and Ariarathes IV of Cappadocia, and invaded Galatia with a large force'; he took territory in Galatia during the early campaign. The page names no places, so the zone is the whole of Cliopatria's Galatia shape.

region.text: Paphlagonia, where Pharnaces took territory in the early campaign

ledger.note: 181: the same campaign takes land in Paphlagonia. 'He took territory in both regions [Galatia and Paphlagonia] during the early campaign.'

region.text: Galatia: all conquests given up

ledger.note: 179: Pharnaces buys peace and gives the conquests back. 'Compelled to purchase peace with the cession of all his conquests in Galatia and Paphlagonia, with the exception of Sinope' after the war that 'ran until summer 179 BC'; the Kingdom page has a treaty with Eumenes of Pergamon and Ariarathes of Cappadocia.

region.text: Paphlagonia: all conquests given up, Sinope excepted

ledger.note: 179: the Paphlagonian conquests are given back with the Galatian ones; Sinope is kept.

region.text: the province of Phrygia

ledger.note: 129: Mithridates V receives Phrygia. He was 'rewarded by the Roman consul Manius Aquillius with the province of Phrygia' for helping Rome against Eumenes III (131-129 BC); the Aristonicus page has Aquillius dividing the former Pergamene kingdom 'among Rome, Pontus, and Cappadocia'. The Mithridates V page gives no exact year for the reward. [Reviewer me-05-d, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from roman-republic to kingdom-of-pergamon so that it mirrors the Kingdom of Pergamon dossier's -129 loss of Phrygia to Pontus; the Aristonicus of Pergamon page has Aquillius 'dividing the Pergamene kingdom among Rome, Pontus, and Cappadocia'.]

region.text: Phrygia, lost when Mithridates V died

ledger.note: c. 120: Phrygia reverts to Rome. The Mithridates V page says he kept Phrygia until his death, assassinated around 120 BC in Sinope, and is silent on what became of it; the return to Rome is a bridging judgement. Review 2026-10-19: the Phrygia page (opened) is silent on Pontus and has only 'In 133 BC, the remnants of Phrygia passed to Rome'; the Roman Republic dossier dates Rome's addition of western Phrygia to 116, four years later. Still a gap.

region.text: Colchis, conquered, and Lesser Armenia, inherited from Antipater

ledger.note: c. 110: Colchis and Lesser Armenia. Paraphrase of the Kingdom of Pontus page, which has no timeline: Mithridates 'began his expansion by inheriting Lesser Armenia from King Antipater (precise date unknown, c.115-106)' and by 'conquering the Kingdom of Colchis' (no year). The year is the middle of the Lesser Armenia range; the Mithridates VI page says he 'first subjugated Colchis' (no date), and the Colchis page has him quelling an uprising in Colchis in 83 BC, so Colchis was Pontic by then. No Cliopatria state holds Colchis after -231, so the counterpart is 'nobody'.

region.text: the Tauric Chersonesus side of Crimea, west of the Kerch peninsula

ledger.note: c. 110: the Tauric Chersonesus. The Chersonesus page has the city 'compelled to call in the aid of Mithradates VI and his general Diophantus, c. 110 BC'; the Kingdom of Pontus page has, undated, 'After various campaigns in the north of the Crimea he controlled all of the Chersonesus', and the Diophantus page (chronology 'disputed') has him relieve the siege of Chersonesos by the Scythian king Palacus, with no year. The year agrees with the Greek City-States dossier's loss of Chersonesus. [Review 2026-10-19: moved from -105 (confidence 1) to -110; region changed from a circle round Chersonesus to the peninsula west of the Kerch circle, so that the Bosporan vassal is not drawn twice.]

region.text: Paphlagonia, divided with Nicomedes III of Bithynia

ledger.note: 108: Mithridates VI and Nicomedes III partition Paphlagonia. 'He contrived to partition Paphlagonia and Galatia with King Nicomedes III of Bithynia'; 'It was probably on the occasion of the Paphlagonian invasion of 108 BC that Mithridates adopted the Bithynian era' (Mithridates VI page; the year is 'probably', and no dividing line is given, so the whole Paphlagonia shape is marked). The Kingdom of Pontus page has the partition ('Mithridates and Nicomedes of Bithynia both invaded Paphlagonia and divided it amongst themselves') but no year; the c. 116 of the first version of this event, and the quotation attached to it, were not on that page. [Review 2026-10-19: moved from -116 to -108.]

region.text: 'part of Galatia that had belonged to his father's kingdom', location not given

ledger.note: 108: part of Galatia. The Mithridates VI page has him partition Paphlagonia and Galatia with Nicomedes III (the 108 BC invasion, 'probably'); the Kingdom of Pontus page says 'Mithridates also took a part of Galatia that had previously been part of his father's kingdom' with no year. Neither names a place, so only the Pontic-Galatian frontier strip is marked; a bridging reading, as in the Galatia dossier. [Review 2026-10-19: moved from -116 to -108.]

region.text: Panticapaeum and the Bosporan Kingdom on the Kerch strait

ledger.note: 107: the Bosporan Kingdom under Mithridates. The Diophantus page: 'Around 107 BC, Mithridates dispatched Diophantes to Panticapaeum', 'persuading the Bosporan king Paerisades V to cede his kingdom to Mithridates'; the Mithridates VI page has the Bosporan Kingdom and the Chersonesus 'readily surrendered their independence in return for Mithridates' promises to protect them against the Scythians' (undated). The Bosporan Kingdom page lists 'Kingdom of Pontus (107 - 63 BC)' and gives no sentence on the cession's year. Drawn as a vassal (lighter tint) until 63, as in the Cimmerian Bosporus dossier. [Review 2026-10-19: moved from -105 (confidence 1) to -107.]

region.text: Cappadocia under Mithridates' son Ariarathes IX

ledger.note: 101: Cappadocia under a Pontic prince. Paraphrase of the Kingdom of Pontus page, which has no timeline: Ariarathes VII 'was murdered in 101 BC before any battle was fought', and 'Mithridates then installed his eight-year-old son, Ariarathes IX of Cappadocia as king, with Gordius as regent' (no year in that sentence). The vassal status is the reading.

region.text: Cappadocia, evacuated at the Senate's order

ledger.note: 97: Rome ends the Pontic hold on Cappadocia. Paraphrase of the Kingdom of Pontus page, which has no timeline: 'In 97 Cappadocia rebelled, but the uprising was swiftly put down by Mithridates'; 'The Roman Senate decreed that Mithridates had to withdraw from Cappadocia and Nicomedes from Paphlagonia' (no year in that sentence); 'the Romans installed Ariobarzanes in Cappadocia' (no year). The decree is undated on the page, so the year is the page's 97 for the rising; the Ariobarzanes I page dates his reign from 95. [Review 2026-10-19: confidence 3 lowered to 2.]

region.text: Cappadocia, invaded by Tigranes

ledger.note: 91: Tigranes invades Cappadocia at Mithridates' urging. The Kingdom of Pontus page: 'In 91/90 BC, while Rome was busy in the Social War in Italy, Mithridates encouraged his new ally and son-in-law' Tigranes, who invaded Cappadocia (sentence cut off by the fetch); the First Mithridatic War page has Tigranes giving the land to Mithridates in 92.

region.text: Cappadocia restored to its king

ledger.note: 90: the invasion is withdrawn. Paraphrase of the Kingdom of Pontus page: 'A Roman army under Manius Aquillius arrived in Asia Minor in 90 BC, prompting Mithridates and Tigranes to withdraw', and the next sentence has Cappadocia and Bithynia 'restored to their respective monarchs'.

region.text: Cappadocia

ledger.note: 90: Mithridates reinvades Cappadocia. The Kingdom of Pontus page: 'Mithridates invaded Cappadocia once again, and Rome declared war' (no year; it follows the 90 BC withdrawal and precedes the 89 war), so the year is a bridging reading. The First Mithridatic War page adds, undated, that Mithridates 'removed Ariobarzanes from Cappadocia a second time after Sulla had left', not mapped here. Recorded as an occupation (hatched), as the Bithynia dossier records its Pontic occupations, until Dardanus in 85. [Review 2026-10-19: gain changed to occupation_start.]

region.text: Bithynia, taken from Nicomedes IV by his brother with Mithridates' help

ledger.note: 90: Nicomedes IV is driven out. The Nicomedes IV page: 'Socrates Chrestus, assisted by Mithridates VI, defeated Nicomedes IV's army in 90 BC, and Nicomedes IV was forced to flee to Italy.' The page credits Socrates Chrestus, so the Pontic hold is a bridging reading, recorded to match the Kingdom of Bithynia dossier's occupation of 90. [Review 2026-10-19: added to mirror that dossier.]

region.text: Bithynia, restored to its king

ledger.note: 90: Rome restores the king. The Kingdom of Pontus page: after the Roman army of Manius Aquillius arrived in 90 BC, 'Cappadocia and Bithynia were restored to their respective monarchs'; the Nicomedes IV page dates his restoration elsewhere to 84 BC. [Review 2026-10-19: added to mirror the Kingdom of Bithynia dossier.]

region.text: Bithynia, invaded by Mithridates in the summer of 89

ledger.note: 89: Mithridates takes Bithynia. The Kingdom of Pontus page: 'In the summer of 89 BC, Mithridates invaded Bithynia and defeated Nicomedes and Aquillius in battle'; the First Mithridatic War page adds that he 'captured Bythinia without opposition' (no year in that sentence), and the Nicomedes IV page has Mithridates retaliating 'again in 88 BC'. The Kingdom of Bithynia dossier dates its Pontic occupation from 88 (confidence 3); 89 is the year the Kingdom page gives, and the two dossiers differ by one year. Recorded as an occupation (hatched) until Dardanus, not as a gain, as the Bithynia dossier does. [Review 2026-10-19: gain changed to occupation_start; the quotation 'late summer of 89' formerly attributed to the First Mithridatic War page is not on that page.]

region.text: the Roman province of Asia: Phrygia, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia, Caria and the Troad, taken 'through Phrygia' in early 88

ledger.note: 88: Roman Asia falls. 'This swift conquest of Asia through Phrygia took place in early 88.' The Ephesian Vespers (late summer or early autumn 88) killed, by the page's figure, up to 80,000 Italians.

region.text: Athens and Boeotia, the Greek front of the war

ledger.note: 88: Athens breaks with Rome. 'Athens, under Athenion, broke with Rome'; Archelaus took Delos and gave Aristion control of Athens. Sulla landed in Epirus in spring 87. The Greek lands were an ally's, not a Pontic province.

region.text: Athens and Attica under Aristion

ledger.note: 88: Athens goes over to Mithridates. The First Mithridatic War page: 'Following the fall of Medeius in 88, the ecclesia voted the dispatch of a delegation' (Athenion's mission) and 'Archelaus sent Aristion to Athens with 2,000 men and the treasure of Apollo, which he used to become tyrant' (no year). The Greek City-States dossier records this as a Pontic occupation from 88. The contest with Rome over the same land is kept (ledger, 88-86). [Review 2026-10-19: added to mirror that dossier.]

region.text: Athens and Boeotia

ledger.note: 86: Sulla wins Greece. 'Athens starved and finally fell on 1 March 86'; Sulla then 'defeated Archelaus at Chaeronea, then at Orchomenos'.

region.text: Athens and Attica

ledger.note: 86: Sulla takes Athens. 'Athens starved and finally fell on 1 March 86' (First Mithridatic War page). [Review 2026-10-19: added to mirror the Greek City-States dossier.]

region.text: the Roman province of Asia: Phrygia, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia, Caria and the Troad, taken 'through Phrygia' in early 88

ledger.note: 85: Dardanus. 'Mithridates surrendered Roman Asia, returned Bithynia and Cappadocia to their kings, paid 2,000 talents, and supplied ships. He kept the rest of his holdings.' The First Mithridatic War page: late summer or early autumn 85, 'in effect a return to the status quo of 89'.

region.text: Bithynia, returned to its king

ledger.note: 85: Dardanus. The Kingdom of Pontus page: Mithridates 'returned Bithynia and Cappadocia to their former kings'; the First Mithridatic War page has the meeting 'in late summer or early autumn 85' and calls the treaty 'in effect a return to the status quo of 89'. Bithynia is evacuated; the occupation (hatched) ends. [Review 2026-10-19: loss changed to occupation_end.]

region.text: Cappadocia, returned to its king

ledger.note: 85: Cappadocia returns to Ariobarzanes (Dardanus): Sulla 'demanded that Mithridates restore the kings of Bithynia and Cappadocia' (First Mithridatic War page). The occupation (hatched) ends. [Review 2026-10-19: loss changed to occupation_end.]

region.text: Bithynia, invaded by Mithridates after Nicomedes IV's bequest to Rome

ledger.note: 74: the Third Mithridatic War opens in Bithynia. 'In 74 BC, King Nicomedes IV of Bithynia died and left his kingdom to Rome'; Mithridates invaded Bithynia and the consul Cotta was defeated at Chalcedon in 74. The page dates the war 73-63; the Mithridates VI page puts the bequest and invasion in 73.

region.text: Bithynia

ledger.note: 72: Bithynia is no longer fought over. The page does not say when Rome retook it; Lucullus's march into Pontus in 72 shifts the war to Mithridates' own kingdom, so the end is a bridging judgement.

region.text: the kingdom of Pontus under Roman occupation: Themiscyra, Amisus, Sinope and the interior

ledger.note: 72: Lucullus invades Pontus. 'In 72 BC, Lucullus marched through Galatia into Pontus'; he besieged Themiscyra and 'later took Amisus and Sinope'; Mithridates lost Cabira 'and fled Pontus' to Tigranes. Occupation of the whole kingdom to 67 is the reading.

region.text: the kingdom of Pontus, regained

ledger.note: 67: Zela. 'In spring 67 BC, Mithridates returned to Pontus while Lucullus was besieging Nisibis in Mesopotamia. At the Battle of Zela, the Romans were defeated, leaving 7,000 dead, and Mithridates regained control of Pontus.'

region.text: the kingdom of Pontus under Roman occupation

ledger.note: 66: Pompey takes command. 'The Lex Manilia passed ... Late in 66 BC, Pompey defeated Mithridates at the river Lycus.' The Kingdom page adds Dasteira and the founding of Nicopolis (66-65). Occupation to the 63 settlement is the reading.

region.text: Colchis, where Mithridates fled and Pompey reached the Phasis

ledger.note: 65: Pompey in Colchis. 'In 65 BC, Pompey campaigned against the Albanians, the Iberians, and Colchis, reaching Phasis'; Mithridates fled from Colchis to Crimea.

region.text: Colchis

ledger.note: 63: Colchis becomes a client kingdom of Rome. 'Colchis became a client kingdom.'

region.text: the kingdom of Pontus as occupied since 66

ledger.note: 63: the occupation ends in the settlement: the western half is annexed and the interior becomes a client kingdom.

region.text: the western half of Pontus including the Greek coast and Sinope

ledger.note: 63: the western half is annexed. The Kingdom of Pontus page: 'Most of the western half of Pontus and the Greek cities of the coast, including Sinope, were annexed by Rome directly' (no year in the sentence; the 63 BC date is the page's lead and infobox) and 'The interior and eastern coast remained an independent client kingdom'. The Bithynia and Pontus page says Pontus 'was simply added to its former competitor, Bithynia'. [Review 2026-10-19: the earlier quotation was a paraphrase.]

region.text: Paphlagonia: the coast to the province, the interior to native princes

ledger.note: 63: Paphlagonia. Pompey 'joined the coastal districts of Paphlagonia to the Roman province of Bithynia et Pontus and left the interior to native princes'; the Paphlagonia page gives no year for the step, the Kingdom page puts the settlement in 63.

region.text: Colchis

ledger.note: 63: Colchis leaves the kingdom as a Roman client state ('Colchis became a client kingdom').

region.text: Lesser Armenia and the part of eastern Pontus on the Galatian frontier, 'location not given'

ledger.note: c. 63: Lesser Armenia and part of eastern Pontus go to Deiotarus. Pompey made him a king; 'the Senate granted him Lesser Armenia and most of Galatia, and he gained part of eastern Pontus' (Deiotarus page, which dates the rewards only between c. 65 and 60). The page names no place for the eastern Pontus part, so the Pontic-Galatian frontier strip is marked, the same band as the Galatia dossier's gain. [Review 2026-10-19: the band added to mirror the Galatia dossier.]

region.text: Panticapaeum and the Bosporan Kingdom

ledger.note: 63: the Bosporan protection ends. Mithridates took the Bosporan throne and had his son Machares killed; Pharnaces II rebelled and Mithridates died at Panticapaeum; the Bosporan Kingdom 'stayed independent under Pharnaces II as a Roman friend' (Kingdom page).

region.text: the Tauric Chersonesus side of Crimea, west of the Kerch peninsula

ledger.note: 63: the Chersonesus side of Crimea leaves the kingdom. Pharnaces II 'stayed independent ... as a Roman friend' (Kingdom page) and held the Bosporan throne (the Kerch peninsula, whose vassalage ends in the previous event). The pages do not say what became of the Tauric Chersonesus: the Chersonesus page says only that the city 'was subject to Rome and received a garrison from the middle of the 1st century BC', and the Bosporan Kingdom page does not mention it, so the transfer to the Bosporan Kingdom is a bridging reading. [Review 2026-10-19: the region no longer includes the Kerch peninsula.]
63: with Sinope in the Roman province, the interior kingdom's seat is taken to be Amaseia; the pages opened do not name a seat for the client kingdom (bridging judgement).

region.text: Pontus, Colchis and Lesser Armenia, overrun by Pharnaces II

ledger.note: 48: Pharnaces II invades. 'Pharnaces II invaded and took Colchis, Lesser Armenia, Pontus, and Cappadocia'; the Deiotarus page has him beating Deiotarus's Galatian legions at Nicopolis in 48.

region.text: Pontus, Colchis and Lesser Armenia, recovered

ledger.note: 47: Zela. 'Caesar then defeated Pharnaces at Zela' (Deiotarus page); the Kingdom page has Caesar defeating him at Zela after he had taken the lands in 48.

37: the Mithridatid line gives way to the Polemonids. The Kingdom page lists Darius 47-37, Arsaces 37 and Polemon I 37-8 BC; the Polemon I page says 'Antony set up client kings in the eastern provinces' in 37 and that Pontus went to Darius at that time, with Polemon's Pontic reign dated 36/37-8. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Lesser Armenia

ledger.note: 31: Lesser Armenia to Polemon I. 'Antony rewarded Polemon with Lesser Armenia' after the alliance with Artavasdes of Media Atropatene was finalised.

region.text: Colchis, conquered by Polemon I

ledger.note: Polemon I's Colchis. The Polemon I page lists 'Colchis, which he conquered' among his lands and says Pythodorida 'ruled Colchis and other regions' after him; it gives no date, so -31 (the year of the Lesser Armenia grant) is a bridging reading and the true year lies between 37 and 8 BC.

region.text: Pontus including Colchis, annexed as a Roman province

ledger.note: 62: Nero annexes Pontus. 'In 62, Nero induced Polemon II to abdicate the Pontic throne'; 'Pontus, including Colchis, became a Roman province.' Polemon II kept only Cilicia until his death in 74. The infobox: 'Dissolved: annexed by the Roman Empire under Nero, 62 AD'.

wars.name: Pharnaces I's war with Pergamon and Cappadocia
wars.outcome: Rome halted the fighting once and talks at Pergamon failed; the war ran to summer 179. Pharnaces had to 'purchase peace with the cession of all his conquests in Galatia and Paphlagonia, with the exception of Sinope'.
wars.note: The Kingdom page dates the treaty to 179 and the capture of Sinope to 182; the Pharnaces I page puts the war at 181-179 and the Pergamon page at c. 183-179.

wars.name: Pontic and Bithynian partition of Paphlagonia and Galatia
wars.outcome: Mithridates VI and Nicomedes III divided Paphlagonia and Mithridates took part of Galatia; in 97 the Senate ordered Nicomedes out of Paphlagonia and Mithridates out of Cappadocia.
wars.note: 108 on the Mithridates VI page ('probably'); the Kingdom of Pontus page gives the partition no year. [Review 2026-10-19: was -116..-108.]

wars.name: Pontic interventions in Cappadocia
wars.outcome: Ariarathes VI murdered at Mithridates' behest (116), Laodice regent to 102, Ariarathes IX installed (101), the 97 rising and the Senate's order that followed, Tigranes' invasion at Mithridates' urging (91/90) and the restoration of 90; Mithridates reinvaded and Rome declared war.

wars.name: First Mithridatic War

zones.text: the Roman province of Asia: Phrygia, Mysia, Lydia, Ionia, Caria and the Troad, taken 'through Phrygia' in early 88

wars.outcome: Roman victory: 'Mithridates formally accepted Sulla's terms'; Roman Asia, Bithynia and Cappadocia returned, a 'return to the status quo of 89'. The Senate never ratified the treaty.
wars.note: The Kingdom page and Cliopatria draw the war from 89; the war page dates the outbreak to late summer 89.

wars.name: Second Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Murena attacked; Mithridates beat his legions at the Halys in 82 and peace was declared again; no border moved.

wars.name: Third Mithridatic War

zones.text: the kingdom of Pontus, occupied 72-67 and again from 66

wars.outcome: Roman victory: Lucullus took Pontus (72), Mithridates regained it at Zela (67), Pompey beat him (66) and annexed the western half in 63 while the interior became a client kingdom; Mithridates died at Panticapaeum in 63.
wars.note: The war page dates it 73-63 but the invasion of Bithynia and Cotta's defeat to 74.

wars.name: Pharnaces II's campaign and Zela
wars.outcome: Pharnaces II overran Colchis, Lesser Armenia, Pontus and Cappadocia in 48 and was beaten by Caesar at Zela in 47.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines survive in the pages opened; the only treaty frontiers (Pharnaces I's 179 peace, Dardanus 85, Pompey's 63 settlement) are described by lands, not lines, so every frontier is soft.

notes: Pages: nine opened (budget 9); every event cites one of them. Cliopatria rows: (1) the -126..-78 shapes put all of Galatia (-127 shape, 181 cells), Paphlagonia (-127 shape, 81 cells) and a Lycaonia block (123 cells, Konya and Isparta; the same block Cliopatria's Galatia -77 shape adds) inside Pontus; none of the pages opened gives Pontus Galatia or Lycaonia, so the corrections subtract Cliopatria's Galatia -77 shape; the Paphlagonia cells are kept only from 108 (partition) and are dropped in 63. (2) The -87..-78 shape is the First Mithridatic War conquest (Bithynia, Cappadocia, Roman Asia and a sliver of Attica) held 8 years too long: Dardanus (85) restored the pre-war kingdom, so the new keyframe -84 applies from -84. (3) Colchis and Crimea enter Cliopatria in -91; the pages place Lesser Armenia in c. 115-106, Colchis undated before 83, the Chersonesus c. 110 (Chersonesus page) and the Bosporan cession c. 107 (Diophantus page). (4) Cliopatria's -63..67 client kingdom lacks Colchis and Lesser Armenia, which the Polemonid pages add; the Polemon I page dates Colchis' conquest to no year, so Colchis' entry is confidence 1. (5) The kingdom ends in 62 (Polemon II page, infobox), not 67. The Pontic client status after 63 and the vassal relation of Bosporan Kingdom/Cappadocia are one-sided in the schema: vassal_start names the vassal as counterpart, so the Roman Republic/Empire dossiers must carry 'vassal_start kingdom-of-pontus' for 63 BC-62 AD (not recorded here). Disagreements: Sinope 183 (Paphlagonia page, quoted) or 182 (Kingdom page); the Pharnaces I page cannot say which year; Paphlagonia partition: no year on the Kingdom page (an earlier version gave c. 116 from a quotation that is not on it), 108 on the Mithridates VI page; the Senate's order on Cappadocia 97 (Kingdom page) against Ariobarzanes I's reign from 95 (his page); the Bithynia bequest 74 (Third War page) or 73 (Mithridates VI page). The Kingdom of Pontus page gives no infobox area, so the area check could not be done; Cliopatria's 80 k km2 for the client kingdom and 585 k km2 at the 88-85 peak are unverified. Not covered by any page opened: the extent of the 'part of Galatia' taken in 108; what Rome did with Phrygia after Mithridates V; Pontus's fate under Darius and Arsaces (47-37); the client kingdom's seat after 63 (capital entry is a bridging judgement); the Cilician lands of Polemon II (not contiguous, not mapped). A gap-filler should open the pages 'Pharnacia', 'Amaseia', 'Pontus (region)' and 'Pontus Polemoniacus' for the capital and shape after 63, and 'Mithridates VI of Pontus' sub-articles for Crimea. Gazetteer: every region name used resolves; Amastris, Cotyora and Pharnacia are not in the gazetteer and are covered by difference-shapes of Cliopatria's own shapes, Sinop and Chersonesus by places. REVIEW REPAIR 2026-10-19 (author, after the adversarial review): (1) The Paphlagonia and Galatia partition moved from c. 116 to 108: the Kingdom of Pontus page has no timeline and no year for it, the Mithridates VI page has the 108 BC invasion ('probably'); keyframes -120 (extended to -111), -110 (-110..-109, without Paphlagonia) and -108 (-108..-92, with it) replace the old -116 and -105 keyframes. (2) Phrygia 129 now names kingdom-of-pergamon (the reviewer's fix, kept). (3) The Kerch peninsula (circle of 90 km round 36.5 E 45.3 N) is subtracted from every direct Crimea shape (keyframes -110, -108, -91, -87, -84, -77, -66; ledger -110 and -63), since it is a vassal from 107 to 63. The Chersonesus gain moved from -105 (confidence 1) to -110 (Chersonesus page, confidence 2) and the Bosporan protection from -105 to -107 (Diophantus page, confidence 2). (4) Bithynia 89-85 and Cappadocia 90-85 are now occupation_start/occupation_end (hatched), not gain/loss, as in the Kingdom of Bithynia dossier; the -90 Bithynian occupation and the Athens occupation 88-86 (greek-city-states) were added to mirror it. Disagreement kept: the Bithynia dossier starts its occupation in 88, this one in 89 (Kingdom of Pontus page: 'In the summer of 89 BC, Mithridates invaded Bithynia'; the Nicomedes IV page: Mithridates retaliates 'again in 88 BC'); the First Mithridatic War page gives no year for 'captured Bythinia without opposition'. No Cappadocia dossier existed on 2026-10-19 to agree with. (5) Galatia 63: the loss of Lesser Armenia now includes the same Pontic-Galatian frontier band as the Galatia dossier's gain. (6) Notes that looked like page quotations but were summaries (ledger 13, 16-20, 36) are marked as paraphrases and replaced by the sentences read again on 2026-10-19; the 97 vassal_end is lowered to confidence 2 because the Senate decree is undated on the page. (7) Thin items tried: Phrygia (silent on Pontus; Rome's retaking stays -120, confidence 1, against the Roman Republic dossier's 116); Diophantus (107 for the Bosporus, Chersonesos relief undated); Colchis (uprising of 83; conquest and Polemon I's rule undated); Bosporan Kingdom (silent on the Chersonesus, so its fate in 63 stays a bridging reading); Third Mithridatic War (no year for the retaking of Bithynia: 72 stays confidence 1; 'Lucullus marched his army through Galatia and into Pontus' is dated 72). Not mapped: the First Mithridatic War page's undated 'removed Ariobarzanes from Cappadocia a second time after Sulla had left'. The Second Mithridatic War is 83 to 82 on the Kingdom page (the war entry keeps -83..-81 from the Mithridates VI page).
